reviews.title: Data collection issue + Unpleasant Bait and Switch
reviews.text:
The app was promoted as free with no ads. Surprise surprise, you now have to be or deal with ads. 
Should have been honest from the start. This bait & switch strategy is nasty.

Despite the App Store page saying it doesn't collect data. They include a link to a document that goes completely against this. The EULA includes a vague and overly broad clause regarding data collection that raises several red flags for privacy-minded users. It states that the developer may gather “technical data and related information, including but not limited to” details about your device, system, and software. The “including but not limited to” wording effectively gives the licensor wide discretion over what can be collected, and nowhere does the agreement specify limits, retention periods, user rights, or the exact categories of data involved.

Although the clause claims the data will be used only in a “non-personally identifiable” form, this is neither clearly defined nor guaranteed under modern standards like the UK GDPR. De-identified data can often be re-identified or linked back to an individual when combined with other datasets, and the EULA contains no safeguards, opt-outs, or transparency commitments. The purpose limitation is also weak, allowing the licensor to use your data to “improve products” or “provide services,” which in practice can justify a very wide range of secondary uses.

Overall, the agreement gives the developer broad rights to collect and reuse data with minimal clarit
